paras: The threatened lynching of John Robinson took place near Hagerstown, Maryland, in August 1880, when Robinson, a Black man, was captured after leaving a farm near Clearspring with the wife and five children of a white farmer named Key. According to a Baltimore dispatch, there were threats of lynching him, but he was safely jailed at Hagerstown. Papers in Washington, Memphis and West Virginia carried the case as a short news item.

Key was a farmer who lived west of Clearspring, Maryland, and the Baltimore dispatch indicates that Robinson had been with him for the past year. That account says an intimacy grew between Robinson and Mrs. Key, described as a young married woman, and that the two planned to leave together.

A day or two before the dispatch of August 20, Robinson and Mrs. Key left with her five children in Key's wagon, taking groceries and household goods. When the wagon broke down, Robinson found another vehicle and continued toward Pennsylvania, but the party was chased and captured. The capture caused "considerable excitement" at Hagerstown, and the dispatch reported "threats of lynching" against Robinson without saying who made them.

Robinson was committed to jail at Hagerstown on a charge of stealing from Key his wife, five children, a horse, a spring wagon and a lot of flour and bacon. Mrs. Key and the children returned to her husband's home. No report of a trial or further proceedings against Robinson was found in the coverage.

The Washington Evening Star of August 21 ran a single sentence under the heading "Stealing a Man's Wife and Children," calling Robinson "a mulatto" and framing the case as the theft of a white man's family and property. The Shepherdstown Register reprinted the same sentence on September 4 in a column of regional briefs. The Memphis Daily Appeal of August 24 printed the longer Baltimore special under "Eloping With a Negro" in a round-up of crime news, called the pair "the guilty couple," and alone mentioned the lynching threats. No coverage of the case was found in the Black press.

reader.title: Threatened lynching of John Robinson
bases: A2 reports 'threats of lynching' against Robinson after his capture, but he was jailed and no attack is reported; A1 and A3 report only the arrest and charge.

Robinson was not killed: A2 says that despite threats of lynching he was safely jailed at Hagerstown, and A1 reports him committed to jail. No group, act, or stated pretext of the threateners is described.

The arrest and charge are reported in two differently worded items (A1, A2), but the lynching threat, the only violent element, appears only in the Baltimore special printed by the Memphis Daily Appeal (A2); A3 reprints A1.

The Memphis Daily Appeal printed the Baltimore special under 'Eloping With a Negro' inside a crime round-up, calling the pair 'the guilty couple' and mentioning the lynching threats without comment.
